content.title: About
content.content: Salsa is a flavorful sauce made from tomatoes, peppers, onion, garlic and spices, popular in Mexican cuisine. It has a bright, slightly spicy taste and can be used as a dip, dressing, or accompaniment to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salsa is prepared from fresh ingredients and usually not cooked, preserving most vitamins.
There are several types of salsa: fresh (pico de gallo), cooked, fruit‑based (mango or pineapple) and hot varieties.
Tomatoes, the main ingredient, are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Salsa is commonly served with corn chips but also works as a marinade for meat and fish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes and peppers provide vitamin C, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Salsa is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and quercetin from onions have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Capsaicin from hot peppers stimulates gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: The vegetable components add a modest amount of fiber, beneficial for gut health.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: Very hot salsa can cause heartburn or stomach irritation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some people may be allergic to tomatoes, onion or garlic.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Commercial salsa often contains high salt levels; those with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If left at room temperature too long after opening, salsa can develop bacterial growth. Follow storage guidelines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use salsa as a dip for chips, add it to tacos, burritos, salads, soups, or as a marinade for meat and fish. It also pairs well with scrambled eggs and vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store salsa in the refrigerator in a sealed jar for up to 7‑10 days. After opening, keep it cold and avoid cross‑contamination. Discard if it develops an off‑smell, discoloration, or signs of fermentation.
